::: {.section-block}
## Coding

I build small tools and data projects for fun, usually when a question I'm
curious about turns out to need some computing to answer.

**[City Streets](/city-streets/)** is the big one. It treats every city's street
network as a probability measure on $\mathbb{RP}^2$ — compass bearing crossed
with grade — and extends Boeing's orientation-entropy idea into 3D. It computes
rotation-aligned Wasserstein and Jensen–Shannon distances between **84 world
cities**, along with comparable measures of hilliness, walkability, on-street
parking, and staircase-street censuses. It's a Julia package with an interactive
dashboard.

[Open the interactive dashboard →](/city-streets/) ·
[Read more about the project →](projects/city-streets.qmd)
:::

::: {.section-block}
## Leatherwork

I make things out of vegetable-tanned leather — wallets, belts, small goods —
cutting, stitching, and finishing everything by hand. It's the same appeal as a
clean proof: a small number of simple operations, done carefully, composing into
something that holds together.

## Boots

I'm into heritage boots and the long, slow way they age — how a pair takes on the
shape and marks of the person wearing them. That patina is the whole point, and
I've spent a fair bit of time coaxing it along.
